Your data stays on your device
ORBIT keeps your planner on your device and works offline. The internet is used only for ads, the consent form and remote settings. Here is exactly what that means.
Your tasks, projects, notes, habits, goals and app settings are saved in a database on this device only. They are never uploaded to us or to any ad network.
You never have to sign up or sign in. There is no profile and no email address to give us.

ORBIT shows ads served by Google AdMob. To show and measure ads, Google may process your device advertising ID, IP address and approximate location, as described in Google privacy policy. You can reset or limit the advertising ID in your Android settings. ORBIT itself runs no analytics or crash reporting and never reads your tasks or notes for advertising. Ads can be removed with premium once it is available.

ORBIT requests the INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE permissions. They are used only to check whether you are online, to load ads, to show the consent form (your privacy choices) and to fetch app settings. Every planner feature keeps working offline, and no ad is requested while you are offline. Where it applies, you can change your ad consent in Settings under Privacy options.
Besides the internet access described above, ORBIT asks for two permissions, both for reminders:
Lets ORBIT show your task reminders. You can say no and the rest of the app still works.
Lets ORBIT re-schedule your reminders after your phone restarts. It is used for nothing else.
Backup files are plain JSON files saved where you choose. They are NOT encrypted, so anyone who can open the file can read it. Store them somewhere safe.
Android cloud backup and automatic backup of ORBIT\'s data are turned off. Your data only leaves the device when you export it yourself.
Uninstalling ORBIT removes all of its data from your device. To start fresh without uninstalling, restore a backup that contains no data.
